title: anyio 4.15.0 removed from_thread, so every server request returns 500 (/health included); exclude that release
answers: mlflow server not ready, helm install context deadline exceeded
AttributeError module anyio has no attribute from_thread
mlflow model server all requests fail with internal error
body:
Symptom: the MLflow tracking server returns HTTP 500 on every request, including /health, so Kubernetes readiness never passes and helm install --wait times out after a fresh pip install.
Root cause: anyio 4.15.0 dropped from_thread from its top-level lazy-import shim. mlflow/server/fastapi_app.py wraps the Flask app with starlette's WSGI bridge, whose WSGIResponder.start_response calls anyio.from_thread.run, so the call raises AttributeError.
Fix pattern: declare anyio as a direct dependency with a major-version cap and an unsupported entry for the broken release (requirements/skinny-requirements.yaml anyio block, mirrored into pyproject.toml and libs/skinny/pyproject.toml as anyio<5,>=3.6.2,!=4.15.0).
Constraints: this is a bound on anyio, not a code change to the WSGI wrapper. Lift the exclusion only after confirming the starlette bridge works with the newer anyio. The description reports the cause from a failing CI run, not from a reproduction in this diff.
applies: Dependency bounds for anyio in mlflow-skinny and mlflow; relevant when anyio or starlette versions change.
says: Tracking server returns an internal server error on every request after fresh installation
Kubernetes deployment never becomes ready and times out waiting for server health check
Server status endpoint returns five hundred error immediately following a new release install
Cluster container startup fails health probe and times out during automated deployment
Prevent tracking server from crashing on all incoming requests due to incompatible background libraries
search: anyio 4.15.0 removed from_thread from its lazy-import shim, causing starlette's WSGI bridge in mlflow/server/fastapi_app.py:fastapi_app to raise AttributeError and return HTTP 500 on all requests including /health. In requirements/skinny-requirements.yaml, pyproject.toml, and libs/skinny/pyproject.toml, anyio must be bounded to anyio<5,>=3.6.2,!=4.15.0. This is a dependency pin rather than a code change to the WSGI wrapper, and the exclusion must remain until the starlette bridge is confirmed to work with newer anyio.
